doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Dillard University and a Columbia Records digression
title: Self-production, and what record producers actually did
summary: Walton says labels' singles era is fading and he likes to produce himself; he and Brower joke that producers like Orrin Keepnews and Teo Macero mostly asked if you wanted another take.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Is that a good thing or a bad thing?

Oh, it works both ways because uh, uh, if you, uh, uh, can, uh, get the finances to uh go into the studio and do a session, you can sell it online. Better than waitin' on somebody to distribute it into a store.
But you don't have the almighty producer, you know, directing, telling you what to do, 'cause …

[laughs] Now I know you're joking. [laughs] Ahmad Jamal says a producer's job is just to go get coffee. But I hope he doesn't mind me quoting him because it's a hearsay. I didn't hear him say it, so don't let that out, please. [laughs]
[inaudible – overlapping voices]
No, but I, I've …
What's your opinion on the subject?
A producer?
What's your opinion on the subject?

I like to produce, uh, myself. You see a lot of my uh, CDs or whatever produced, uh, by Cedar Walton. And in my case with the HighNote Records, that's just in name only. There's not another, uh, not another level of anything… but nobody knows better than you what you want with your music, you know. We have uh, we don't have the producer in the producer sense like uh … what years were these?
[inaudible - overlapping voices]
In the '70s.
Like Orrin Keepnews.
Yeah, right. Yeah, right. I uh, I, I, was …
Teo Macero.
Right. I was on, I was on sessions with each of these people, and they just ask you, "You wanna do another one?" [laughs] Stuff like that, as I recall, you know.
They didn't hear, they didn't hear when you played a bad note and say, "Go back and do it?"

No, most of the engineers would, would, would tell them that and then they would make believe they'd thought of it – in my opinion. I don't want to give the impression that I have a bad uh, uh [laughs] taste for uh …
We’re just tryin’ get the record straight here.
[laughs] Brower:We wanna get the record straight.
